title: Getting started with survkit
text: Weibull accelerated-failure-time model lung-cancer data: survkit_tidy() gives coefficient table ratios confidence intervals; survkit_curve() gives predicted survival time grid.
code: fit <- survkit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, survival::lung,                method = "weibull") fit #> <survkit_fit> method = weibull (parametric, via flexsurv) #>   n = 228   events = 165 #>   power: ok (82.5 events/predictor) #>   coefficients: #>   shape   scale     age     sex  #>  0.2823  6.2749 -0.0123  0.3821 survkit_tidy(fit) #>    term component    estimate   std_error ratio_type     ratio  conf_low #> 1 shape auxiliary  0.28229534 0.061883272       <NA>        NA        NA #> 2 scale auxiliary  6.27485306 0.481366950       <NA>        NA        NA #> 3   age covariate -0.01225703 0.006957472         TR 0.9878178 0.9744389 #> 4   sex covariate  0.38208514 0.127476840         TR 1.4653368 1.1413767 #>   conf_high #> 1        NA #> 2        NA #> 3  1.001380 #> 4  1.881248 survkit_curve(fit, times = c(100, 300, 500)) #>   time     value profile #> 1  100 0.8618418       1 #> 2  300 0.5282034       1 #> 3  500 0.2846043       1

Kaplan-Meier survival age group (lung cancer trial). confidence bands pointwise 95 percent intervals. older group’s curve sits younger group’s whole follow-, single time-invariant hazard time ratio defensible summary – curves neither cross converge. two curves separate within first 100 days gap holds point risk set thin say – crossing signal genuinely time-varying age effect.

code: mg <- survival::mgus2 mg$etime <- with(mg, ifelse(pstat == 1, ptime, futime)) mg$event <- with(mg, factor(ifelse(pstat == 1, "pcm",                             ifelse(death == 1, "death", "censor")),                             levels = c("censor", "pcm", "death"))) fg <- survkit(survival::Surv(etime, event) ~ age + sex, mg,               method = "fine_gray", cause = "pcm") survkit_tidy(fg) #>   term component    estimate   std_error ratio_type     ratio  conf_low #> 1  age covariate -0.01730171 0.005528135         HR 0.9828471 0.9722555 #> 2 sexM covariate -0.25975679 0.181707036         HR 0.7712391 0.5401567 #>   conf_high #> 1 0.9935541 #> 2 1.1011801

title: Getting started with survkit
text: competing risks Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence event one call, accounts competing event rather treating censoring: Stacking two causes’ cumulative incidence shows much total event probability accounts time, confirms two curves sum proper (non-decreasing, bounded) overall failure probability: Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence plasma-cell malignancy death, stacked top line overall failure probability. Death dominates overall event probability throughout follow-, pcm’s cumulative incidence rises far slowly – exactly separation Fine-Gray hazard summarising.
code: ci <- survkit_cuminc(survival::Surv(etime, event) ~ 1, mg) head(ci) #>   time group cause         cif      cif_se #> 1    1   all   pcm 0.000000000 0.000000000 #> 2    2   all   pcm 0.001446164 0.001021853 #> 3    3   all   pcm 0.001446164 0.001021853 #> 4    4   all   pcm 0.002169246 0.001251056 #> 5    5   all   pcm 0.002892329 0.001444071 #> 6    6   all   pcm 0.003615411 0.001613935 pcm <- ci[ci$cause == "pcm", c("time", "cif")] death <- ci[ci$cause == "death", c("time", "cif")] grid_t <- sort(unique(c(pcm$time, death$time))) pcm_y <- stats::approx(pcm$time, pcm$cif, xout = grid_t, method = "constant",                        rule = 2)$y death_y <- stats::approx(death$time, death$cif, xout = grid_t,                          method = "constant", rule = 2)$y plot(grid_t, pcm_y + death_y, type = "s", col = "#7570b3", lwd = 2,     xlab = "Days", ylab = "Cumulative incidence",     main = "Stacked cumulative incidence: pcm and death",     ylim = c(0, max(pcm_y + death_y))) lines(grid_t, pcm_y, type = "s", col = "#1b9e77", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", legend = c("pcm", "pcm + death"),       col = c("#1b9e77", "#7570b3"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

text: restricted mean survival time (RMST) horizon τ\tau area survival curve [0,τ][0, \tau], RMST(τ)=∫0τS(t)dt,\mathrm{RMST}(\tau) = \int_0^{\tau} S(t)\,dt, summary stays defined median never reached: Predictions can scored discrimination calibration. concordance index, censoring-weighted (IPCW) Brier score, index prediction accuracy returned together. Brier score horizon tt weights subject inverse probability censored tt, BS(t)=1n∑=1n[(0−Ŝ(t∣xi))2Ĝ(Ti)𝟏(Ti≤t,δi=1)+(1−Ŝ(t∣xi))2Ĝ(t)𝟏(Ti>t)], BS(t) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^n \left[   \frac{\big(0-\hat S(t\mid x_i)\big)^2}{\hat G(T_i)}\,   \mathbf{1}(T_i \leq t,\ \delta_i = 1) +   \frac{\big(1-\hat S(t\mid x_i)\big)^2}{\hat G(t)}\,   \mathbf{1}(T_i > t) \right],  Ŝ\hat S predicted survival probability Ĝ\hat G Kaplan-Meier estimator censoring distribution (Graf et al. 1999); index prediction accuracy, IPA(t)=1−BS(t)/BS0(t)IPA(t) = 1 - BS(t)/BS_0(t), rescales covariate-free reference BS0BS_0:
code: km <- survkit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1, survival::lung, method = "km") survkit_rmst(km, tau = 365) #>   tau group     rmst       se conf_low conf_high #> 1 365   all 263.2219 7.798859 247.9364  278.5073 survkit_score(cox, survival::lung, times = c(200, 400, 600)) #>   time   cindex     brier        ipa #> 1  200 0.602853 0.2094928 0.03700922 #> 2  400 0.602853 0.2318152 0.01245320 #> 3  600 0.602853 0.1646295 0.01890319

title: Getting started with survkit
text: Fitting question several ways consistency check survkit built : methods make different distributional assumptions hazard still land near restricted mean survival time. disagree threshold relative spread, fit flagged – either shape hazard misspecified least one methods, compared quantities actually estimand (marginal curve compared curve reference covariate profile, instance). flag prompt check two , verdict : Plotting method’s restricted mean point, disagreement band drawn threshold around mean, makes table easier read glance – “triangulation fan” single picture shown real disagreement immediately, rather requiring table lookup: Triangulation fan: restricted mean survival time tau = 500 days three methods, shaded band spanning mean plus minus half relative-spread threshold. three estimates fall inside band, matching printed flagged = FALSE verdict – weibull, Cox Kaplan-Meier concur within tolerance fit.
code: tri <- survkit_triangulate(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex,                            survival::lung,                            methods = c("weibull", "cox", "km"), tau = 500) tri$rmst #>    method tau     rmst #> 1 weibull 500 311.5567 #> 2     cox 500 312.7260 #> 3      km 500 310.3344 tri$flagged #> [1] FALSE band_half <- tri$threshold * mean(tri$rmst$rmst) / 2 band_mid <- mean(tri$rmst$rmst) plot(seq_len(nrow(tri$rmst)), tri$rmst$rmst, pch = 19, cex = 1.4,     col = "#1b9e77", xaxt = "n", xlab = "Method", ylab = "RMST (days)",     xlim = c(0.5, nrow(tri$rmst) + 0.5),     ylim = range(c(tri$rmst$rmst, band_mid - band_half, band_mid + band_half)),     main = sprintf("Triangulated RMST at tau = %d", tri$tau)) axis(1, at = seq_len(nrow(tri$rmst)), labels = tri$rmst$method) rect(0.5, band_mid - band_half, nrow(tri$rmst) + 0.5, band_mid + band_half,     col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#7570b3", alpha.f = 0.15), border = NA) abline(h = band_mid, lty = 2, col = "#7570b3")

title: A Unified, Extensible Toolkit for Time-to-Event Analysis
text: unified, extensible toolkit time--event analysis: one interface established R survival stack, cross-method triangulation consistency check top. survkit puts one clean interface established R survival stack — parametric accelerated-failure-time models, Cox proportional hazards, competing risks, recurrent events, frailty, flexible splines, non-parametric Kaplan-Meier baseline — driven extensible method registry new estimators slot without API change. Every fit returns single typed object consistent prediction, summary tidying methods. top fits sits value layer makes survkit methodology rather wrapper: Cross-method triangulation (survkit_triangulate()) reads disagreement methods model-misspecification signal. Decision-relevant estimands — restricted mean survival time (survkit_rmst()) cumulative incidence (survkit_cuminc()). Predictive scoring (survkit_score()) — concordance censoring-weighted Brier score index prediction accuracy. events-per-variable power gate flags models small identify. registry conformance contract (survkit_validate_method()). optional ensemble-manifest emitter composition wider analytics stack. stands alone — siblings optional (Suggests, behind requireNamespace() guards) R CMD check clean none installed.

title: Compute the restricted mean survival time — survkit_rmst
text: restricted mean survival time (RMST) horizon tau: area survival curve [0, tau], decision-relevant summary stays defined median reached. Parametric, spline cure fits use backend's RMST delta-method interval; Cox-family non-parametric fits use area survival::survfit() standard error.

title: Compute the restricted mean survival time — survkit_rmst
text: $$RMST(\tau) = \int_0^{\tau} S(t)\,dt$$ \(S(t)\) (model-based Kaplan-Meier) survival function. Restricting integral \([0, \tau]\) keeps summary defined identifiable observed follow-even survival curve never crosses one-half.

title: Compute the restricted mean survival time — survkit_rmst
code: fit <- survkit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1, survival::lung, method = "km") survkit_rmst(fit, tau = 365) #>   tau group     rmst       se conf_low conf_high #> 1 365   all 263.2219 7.798859 247.9364  278.5073

title: Score a fit's predictions — survkit_score
text: data frame time, cindex (Harrell's C using predicted risk horizon), brier (IPCW Brier) ipa (index prediction accuracy).

title: Score a fit's predictions — survkit_score
text: inverse-probability--censoring-weighted Brier score horizon \(t\) $$BS(t) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^n \Big[   \frac{\big(0 - \hat S(t \mid x_i)\big)^2}{\hat G(T_i)}   \mathbf{1}(T_i \le t, \delta_i = 1) +   \frac{\big(1 - \hat S(t \mid x_i)\big)^2}{\hat G(t)}   \mathbf{1}(T_i > t) \Big]$$ \(\hat S(\cdot \mid x_i)\) predicted survival probability, \(\hat G\) Kaplan-Meier estimator censoring survival function, index prediction accuracy \(IPA(t) = 1 - BS(t) / BS_0(t)\) covariate-free reference \(BS_0\).

title: Score a fit's predictions — survkit_score
text: Graf E, Schmoor C, Sauerbrei W, Schumacher M. Assessment comparison prognostic classification schemes survival data. Statistics Medicine 1999; 18(17-18): 2529-2545. doi:10.1002/(SICI)1097-0258(19990915/30)18:17/18<2529::AID-SIM274>3.0.CO;2-5

title: Score a fit's predictions — survkit_score
code: fit <- survkit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, survival::lung,                method = "cox") survkit_score(fit, survival::lung, times = c(200, 400, 600)) #>   time   cindex     brier        ipa #> 1  200 0.602853 0.2094928 0.03700922 #> 2  400 0.602853 0.2318152 0.01245320 #> 3  600 0.602853 0.1646295 0.01890319

title: survkit 0.1.0
text: survkit_tidy() longer exponentiates parametric fit’s baseline parameters meaningless ratio, now labels covariate effect scale. output gains component column ("covariate" / "auxiliary") ratio_type column ("HR" / "TR" / "" / probit). survkit_curve() returns predicted quantity column named value (survival), function now predicts hazard, cumulative hazard quantiles well survival.
code: # before: shape and scale were listed as covariates with a bogus "ratio" #   term  estimate  ratio #   scale 6.27      531.0        <- exponentiated log-scale intercept #   sex   0.38      1.47         <- a time ratio, unlabelled  # after: auxiliaries are separated, covariates carry their ratio type #   term  component  estimate  ratio_type  ratio #   scale auxiliary  6.27      <NA>        NA #   sex   covariate  0.38      TR          1.47

title: survkit 0.1.0
text: survkit_triangulate() fits data several methods reads relative spread restricted mean (, optionally, survival landmark) model-misspecification signal. survkit_rmst() computes restricted mean survival time horizon, backend’s interval parametric fits survival package’s standard error Cox-family non-parametric fits. survkit_cuminc() gives Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence competing event. survkit_score() scores predictions Harrell’s concordance inverse-probability--censoring-weighted Brier score index prediction accuracy. survkit_contract() survkit_validate_method() expose check registry conformance contract every fit closure must honour. New methods registry: km (Kaplan-Meier / Nelson-Aalen non-parametric baseline) cox_ridge (ridge-penalised Cox -events regime). survkit_curve() gains type argument ("survival", "hazard", "cumhaz", "quantile"). as_survkit_manifest() now emits genuine per-draw survival ensemble parametric, spline cure fits (draws survival share one sample); Cox-family fits emit maximum-likelihood curve marked draw = 0. survkit() gains on_underpowered = c("warn", "abstain") argument. "warn" preserves historical behaviour (fit anyway, warning); "abstain" declines fit -powered model instead returns [survkit_refusal()] – typed, classed token (c("survkit_refusal", "orchestra_refusal", "error", "condition")) recognisable leader-side gate via is_orchestra_decline(), rather bare warning() plus fitted model regardless power gate’s verdict.

title: survkit 0.1.0
text: power gate returns "unknown" multi-state (competing-risks) response rather pooling competing events one misleading count. Cox-family fits retain model frame (model = TRUE), survival curves scoring new data work reliably. survkit_fit carries ratio_type aux_pars tidier can separate covariate effects baseline parameters backend.

title: survkit 0.1.0
text: Vignette (Getting started survkit) gains three figures captions interpretive prose: Kaplan-Meier curve age group, stacked cumulative-incidence plot competing-risks example, “triangulation fan” plotting method’s restricted mean survival time disagreement band. also states governing equations events-per-variable gate, restricted mean survival time IPCW Brier score, source citation, rewords triangulation section longer asserts flagged disagreement proves model misspecification (can also arise comparing different estimands, vignette now says explicitly). README.md leads package’s purpose first lines, every code snippet now self-contained runnable end--end survival::lung / survival::mgus2 (Fine-Gray, small-sample-gate scoring snippets previously referenced undefined objects). Roxygen: several @titles rewritten sentences/imperatives rather noun phrases (survkit_power, survkit_fit, survkit_manifest, survkit_contract, survkit_cuminc, survkit_rmst, survkit_curve); @examples added survkit_fit, survkit_manifest predict method fit (previously undocumented example); @references added survkit_power survkit_score; governing-equation @details added survkit_rmst survkit_score.
